tonight.headline: Sadiq's injury is his back, and Tuten is back in the flex
body: Week 4 hasn't started for you; nobody on your roster plays tonight. ESPN has you at 123.2 against Team 13's 112.3, 55%. The bad news: Kenyon Sadiq, your only tight end, was limited Wednesday and the Jets' report names it — a back injury.

One small thing to do: the lineup was changed at 03:31 to put Tuten in the flex over Downs. The projection prefers Downs by a point. It's a coin flip, so take the projection (card 1). If Sadiq is ruled out, Mark Andrews is now a free agent — no priority needed.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Team 13 start Josh Allen, who practised without issue (CBS). DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and their RB2 Rachaad White (shoulder) both missed Wednesday (PhiladelphiaEagles.com; NBC and Hogs Haven headlines); Lamar Jackson, on their bench, also sat out (Heavy).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Smith and White both ruled out Friday: Team 13 lose two starters unless they fill from Moore and Corum, and your win probability rises.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sun 07:30 Mexico City (Downs locks in London)
doFirst.title: Put Downs back in the flex over Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: 13.7 to 12.7. A coin flip, so it goes to the projection — and no thesis.

case.label: The rule
case.body: lineup_check.py: 'start Josh Downs 13.7 over Bhayshul Tuten 12.7 — COIN FLIP, take the projection.' Neither has news ESPN hasn't priced: both are off their Wednesday reports (Colts via Yahoo; Jaguars.com).

case.label: The player
case.body: Downs has 30.4% of Indianapolis' targets since Pierce went out (Sharp), and Washington allow a league-high 24.8 passing points a game.

case.label: The timing cost
case.body: Downs locks at 07:30 in London, Tuten at 11:00. Putting Downs in the flex gives up a little late flexibility, but nothing on this roster is waiting on a later inactive except Sadiq, and only a tight end covers him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Tuten outscores Downs. It's a coin flip: this is the expected-value call, not a prediction, and it gets no decision-log entry.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · if Sadiq is ruled out Friday or inactive at Sun 09:30 Mexico City
doFirst.title: If Sadiq sits: add Mark Andrews, drop Carnell Tate
doFirst.subtitle: Carried. Andrews cleared waivers overnight, so it's a free add — no priority.

case.label: The injury
case.body: The Jets' official Wednesday report lists Sadiq limited with a back injury, alongside Ruckert (knee); Mason Taylor DNP again (NewYorkJets.com 30 Sep). ESPN: QUESTIONABLE at 9.9.

case.label: The fallback
case.body: Andrews projects 10.1 at home to Tennessee, whose top two backs, Pollard and Spears, missed Wednesday (TennesseeTitans.com). Zay Flowers was limited with the hamstring (Yahoo), so Andrews' share could shrink if Flowers is full go. He's a FREEAGENT in this snapshot: an add, not a claim.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Carnell Tate, the fifth receiver and not on the screen's exposure list. Golden, Kamara and Gordon are, so they are never the drop.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and Andrews scores less than the best free tight end that week (Hunter Henry, Loveland).

whatWentWrong.title: The flex was flipped overnight, away from the projection
whatWentWrong.lead: Downs went into the flex at 20:10 yesterday, then back out for Tuten at 03:31. Two changes to one slot in seven hours, ending a point below the projection.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: Section 0 of the strategy: every Week 1–2 loss was winnable with the roster owned, and the most expensive mistake was overriding the projection. A one-point flip isn't a disaster; the habit is.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: News ESPN hasn't priced about Downs or Tuten. I found none.

whatWentWrong.title: One tight end, now with a named back injury
whatWentWrong.lead: Yesterday it was 'undisclosed'. The Jets' report says back. No bench player can cover the slot.

case.label: The tool
case.body: lineup_check.py: 'NOBODY ELIGIBLE on the bench — find one on the wire.' That's the Andrews card.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Sadiq full on Thursday or Friday: nothing fires.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Steelers 8.2 at Cleveland tonight; the Browns are without both Jenkinses on the line and WR Tylan Wallace (Steelers.com). But Pittsburgh's corners are thin: Porter out, Ramsey questionable with a broken wrist. Ravens 7.3 at home to a Titans team whose top two backs missed Wednesday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing: the seat changed on Wednesday, the gap is inside a point, and the Steelers lock at 18:15 tonight.

doNotChase.name: Keenan Allen
doNotChase.lead: Still the wire's biggest riser, and still the same role reason you already own in Downs.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 25.7% of Indianapolis targets with Pierce on IR (Sharp, carried). Limited Wednesday on a rest day (Colts' report via Yahoo).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Downs, yours, has 30.4% of targets since Pierce went out (Sharp), and 11 to Allen's 9 in Week 3 (archive). Doubling up on one team's vacancy buys nothing.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Downs hurt.

doNotChase.name: Jaylen Wright
doNotChase.lead: The riser splitting the backfield you spent priority on.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Limited Wednesday with the foot (Vikings.com 30 Sep); SI has him ahead of Gordon on the depth chart.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be a fifth back on a roster that starts two, at Minnesota (4th-fewest to RBs, footballdb). A free agent, but a roster seat is still a cost.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wright takes over Miami outright (Gordon under 8 touches) — then Gordon is the problem to solve, not a reason to own both.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage, from three weeks of data, which is still thin. The only wire need is the Sadiq fallback, an injury plan rather than a usage gap.
